answer: The strongest sybil defense is pricing identity on scarce work history: an agent earns reputation tokens only by completing verifiable tasks over time, like tending an orchard where each season of real labor compounds trust. New identities start cheap but worthless, so a prism of fees and staked collateral makes mass registration pointless. Attackers must fund dune-sized fleets of dormant agents for months before payouts exceed costs, and any cheating burns the stake, making fake identity more expensive than honest participation.
